summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol use disorder, chronic pain, and tobacco use, was admitted for hypoxia and acute alcohol intoxication. He presented with shortness of breath, wheezing, and slurred speech, and was found at a train stop. He was treated for COPD exacerbation with prednisone, nebulizers, and levofloxacin, and for alcohol withdrawal with valium and supportive vitamins. His chest X-ray showed bibasilar atelectasis with a right lower lobe opacity concerning for infection. Laboratory results revealed initial leukopenia, hypomagnesemia, and hypernatremia, all of which improved with treatment. He expressed interest in entering a recovery program and was close to securing a placement, but eloped from the hospital at 5:30 AM on hospital day two, before completing detox or receiving discharge instructions.
